## Questions

What is Jackalope?

Jackalope is a desktop workspace for agent-assisted development. It keeps your projects, ideas, agent tasks, isolated Git worktrees, and code review together, so you can follow work from intent to result.

Do I need an AI subscription?

Bring Codex, Claude Code, Grok, or OpenCode. Jackalope uses their installed command-line interfaces; see the agent section for connection and sign-in differences. Provider account requirements, subscriptions, and usage limits still apply. Jackalope does not include model access.

results.title: The Open Source Alternative to Codex & Claude Code
results.content: OpenCode is a AI-powered coding agent that lives inside your terminal or IDE. Unlike cloud-locked tools, it lets you bring your own model from 75 providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Deep Sea, Ollama, and Ollama local, xAI, and dozens more. And gives the AI direct access to your code base through a rich set of built-in tools like file editing, file reading, shell commands, web search, grep, globe, and LSP integration. The core functionality is simple. You describe what you want in natural language, and OpenCode's agent reads your code, plans changes, edits files, runs command, and iterates, all inside your project directory. Key characteristics: fully open source, provider-agnostic, use any LLM via API key or local inference, multi-interface like TUI, CLI, web UI, desktop app, IDE [...] LSP. Auto format code after edits and give the agent code intelligence using LSP. Share conversation. /share creates a link. Great for code review and team discussion. Context compaction. Open code auto compacts long conversations, but you can trigger it manually using /compact. Check stats to see token usage and cost across sessions. That's it. You are ready to ship code and build application with open code. For detailed walk-through, check out this video. See you again. [...] list them clearly. Go to your repo, settings, secrets and variables, Actions. New repository secret. Name give it OpenClaw API key. Value, your Zen API key. Save. Make a small change in another branch and add a deliberate issue to see if OpenCode catches it. Now, create a PR. Go to GitHub. Pull request. New pull request. Select test PR check. Create pull request. Watch the check appear. On the PR page, scroll to the bottom. You will see OpenCode review in progress. OpenCode will also leave a comment on the PR with its detailed review. Supports 75 providers, Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock, Azure, Deep Seek from China, XAI, GitHub Copilot, GitLab Duo, Grok, Ollama local, LM Studio local, Llama CPP, OpenRouter, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Hugging Face, NVIDIA, Cloudflare,

results.content:
And the interesting part is that you don’t have to replace your existing agent.

You can connect OpenWork to Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, or another compatible MCP client and reuse the same capabilities.

That makes the idea much more interesting than just another AI desktop app.

## What Exactly Is OpenWork?

At its simplest, OpenWork is a way to package and share AI capabilities.

AI coding tools are getting better fast. But there’s a problem that becomes obvious once you start using several of them. You end up rebuilding the same setup again and again.

Your Claude Code environment has certain skills. Your Codex setup has its own MCP servers. Cursor has another set of tools. Then there are Google Workspace connections, Microsoft 365 integrations, plugins, and custom workflows.

Moving all of that between machines or sharing it with a teammate can become a mess.

OpenWork is trying to solve that problem.

OpenWork is a free, open-source desktop app designed for sharing AI workflows. Think of it as a shared capability layer that can sit underneath the AI agents you already use.
